$comment: Ceilings for `yarn validate:anatomy-keyboard` (RESIDUAL-12, closing `D-RES11-2`). Every number ratchets DOWN, never up -- the same rule anatomy-parts-ceilings.json follows, and for a sharper reason: a component's `keyboard` table is PUBLISHED (the ownership manifest carries it, component-meta.json joins it, and the docs page renders it as the keyboard section), so a row with nothing behind it is not untidy documentation, it is an accessibility claim that is false. Seeded at the values MEASURED on 4e4e46f with the uncommitted working tree, never above. Population at seeding: 104 anatomy declarations, 19 declaring `keyboard: 'none'`, 85 declaring bindings, 402 binding rows.
$comment.maxUnbackedDeclarations: A declared keyboard binding that NOTHING handles -- not the declaring component's own source, not a compound part the ownership manifest attributes to it, not a component it renders, not a composable it calls, not a Reka primitive it imports (resolved through Reka's own dist import graph), and no native element at the node the row is about whose documented HTML behaviour is that key. This is `D-RES11-2`'s general case. Measured at 32 (RESIDUAL-11), seeded at 28 (RESIDUAL-12, after `DzChip` and `DzTag` each lost two Enter/Space rows that promised an activation neither component has ever implemented), and **ZERO since RESIDUAL-13**, which closed all 28 of RESIDUAL-12 §4's findings F1-F10: 22 rows were IMPLEMENTED (`DzToolbar` 4 + 2 new vertical rows, `DzListItem` 2, `DzCascader` 2, `DzCarousel` 2, `DzTour` 2, `DzTransfer` 2 -- plus 2 more of its rows re-attributed from a citation that was true about a file and false about the claim -- `DzTimePicker` 4, `DzDatePicker` 2, `DzDateRangePicker` 2) and 6 were WITHDRAWN, on `DzColorPicker`, whose six APG `slider` rows described a colour pointer, a saturation axis and a value axis that the component does not have; see its anatomy's keyboard comment for the measurement, the six true rows that replaced them, and the rejected alternative. Ceiling ZERO, and there is no reading above it: a declared key is either implemented or it is not a contract. It may never be raised, because raising it is how the keyboard section of a documentation page quietly stops describing the component. RESIDUAL-14 then audited the 220 citation sites behind those 404 rows and found 52 naming a real file for the WRONG claim, of which 12 were rows nothing could cite because there was nothing to cite: the count went 0 -> 9 and the gate was left RED with the true number rather than a raised ceiling. RESIDUAL-15 closed those 9 to ZERO by making the claims true, not by widening anything -- `DzDataGrid`'s six `apg: 'grid'` cell rows IMPLEMENTED (`useDataGridNavigation`: arrows on both axes with the inline pair mirrored, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown, a roving `tabindex` over the body's cells) plus two new PageUp/PageDown rows declared in the same change; `DzCalendar`'s two `Shift`+page rows IMPLEMENTED (year paging, four lines in `onGridKeydown`); `DzSplitButton`'s `ArrowDown` (trigger) WITHDRAWN, because `DzSplitButtonMenu.vue` slots the consumer's menu and `DzDropdownMenu` already publishes and implements the `menu-button` pattern. See each anatomy's keyboard comment for the measurement and the rejected alternative.
$comment.maxUndeterminedDeclarations: A declared binding whose ownership could not be decided EITHER WAY, because the node that receives the key is somewhere source cannot follow: a `<slot />` the consumer fills, a render function that builds elements with `h()`, a Reka export that did not map to a dist module, or a part emitted outside the walked closure. Undetermined is NOT satisfied -- it is the honest verdict for a question the checker cannot answer, and it is counted separately so that widening the resolution shows up as THIS number falling rather than as `unbacked` rising. Seeded at the 8 measured on 4e4e46f and **ZERO since RESIDUAL-13**, which closed all 8 by the two routes this comment already named. (1) The component came to own the node: `DzOrderList`'s `<character>` row declared APG listbox type-ahead that did not exist anywhere, and `typeAhead` now reads each rendered row's own text -- the label a screen reader announces -- so the slot stopped being the obstacle. (2) The resolution was extended, twice: `renderFunctionNodesIn` turns each `h('tag', { ... })` call into the opening tag it produces so the SAME platform table decides, which settled `DzAnchor`'s `Enter` against the `<a href>` it builds; and a seventh route, `spec`, credits a row ONLY when it would otherwise be undetermined for a `<slot />` reason AND the component's spec asserts that key through `expectKeyboardContract`'s `handled` or `platform` list -- the runtime half that sees the children a consumer supplies. That settled the remaining 6 (`DzCheckboxGroup`, `DzCollapse` x2, `DzFieldArray` x2, `DzRadioGroup`), each with a spec that mounts the component with the controls a consumer would supply. See `specAssertedKeys` for the four conditions and for what the route deliberately does NOT prove. Ceiling ZERO: a row that cannot be decided statically can be decided at runtime, and the two together leave no third place for an answer to hide. RESIDUAL-14 then found that five slot-based containers' closures had been built from docblock `@example` markup -- the consumer's example, not the component's own render -- and once comments stopped being evidence the count went 0 -> 7, with the gate left RED at the true number. RESIDUAL-15 closed all 7: six by the runtime route this comment already names and one by implementation. `DzTransfer`'s `<character>` row became route `own` when the pane gained a real `typeAheadIndex` reading each rendered option's `textContent` (`D-RES14-2`, the `DzOrderList` shape again); `DzSplitButton`'s `Escape` (menu open) was WITHDRAWN with `D-RES14-4`; and the five `Tab` rows -- `DzCheckboxGroup`, `DzRadioGroup`, `DzStepper`, `DzToolbar`, `DzInfiniteScroll` -- are backed through the `spec` route by a new `tabStops: { of, expect }` assertion in `@dzup-ui/testing`. That option is a WIDENING OF THE RESOLUTION, which is exactly what this comment says makes THIS number fall, and it was needed because `platform: ['Tab']` cannot pass: `PLATFORM_OWNERS` credits activation and text entry only, never navigation, so the call RESIDUAL-14 §6 scheduled throws. A `Tab` row claims one of two OPPOSITE shapes -- each node is its own tab stop, or the set is one -- and RESIDUAL-14 §2.2.4 caught one published as the other, which is why the option names the shape, counts the nodes in the order, and drives the key.
$comment.maxUndeclaredHandlers: The reverse drift: a key a component HANDLES that its governing anatomy (its own, or its `parentComponent`'s for a compound part) does not declare. Just as wrong as the forward case and invisible in the same way -- the published table is then incomplete, so a consumer who reads it does not learn that Delete closes the tab. A component that declares `keyboard: 'none'` and handles a key is the loudest instance and the validator says so. Measured at 8 before this batch and CLOSED to 0 within it: DzSpeedDial's four fan-navigation arrows, DzRating's direction-aware ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, and the Delete/Backspace DzTabTrigger has always used to close a tab were all added to their tables. Ceiling ZERO, and there is no reading above it: the code is the thing that exists, so the declaration can always be made to match it in the same change.
